To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel perphenyl carbamated β‐cyclodekstrin based chiral silica stationary phases were synthesized via thiol‐enzyme click chemistry, and the prepared CD‐CSP was successfully used for the separation of 15 racemic compounds.
a new CD‐CSP was successfully prepared by immobilization of perphenylcarbonyl β‐cyclodextin on 3‐mercaptoropryl functionalized silica gel.
the novel perphenylaminocarboxylated β‐cyclodoextrin based CSPs were successfully synthesized by thiol‐ene reaction, and the prepared CSPs were applied to the separation of racemic compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel CD‐CSP via thiol‐en click chemistry, and it provides a novel and facile approach for the preparation of CD‐CPS with well‐defined structures.
the synthesis of novel perphenyldicarbamate β‐CD chiral stationary phases by thiol‐ene chemistry.
the synthesis of novel CD‐CSP by thiol‐ene reaction, and the synthesized CD‐CSP exhibited excellent enantioseparation ability for various racemic compounds under different chromatographic modes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenyl carbamate group on the rims of CDs could improve the separation efficiency of CD‐CPSs.

the novel CD‐CSP was prepared by immobilization of 10‐undecenoic acid‐mono/di‐(perphenylcarbamoyl) β‐CD on mercaptopropyl functional group modified silica gel via thio‐ene click chemistry, and the CSP showed good enantioselectivity and enantiosensitivity for a variety of racemic compounds, which was a novel CD‐CSp with well‐defined molecular structure.
this CD‐CPS with novel structure is promising in the separation of racemic compounds, and the synthesis of CD‐CPS by click chemistry is a facile approach for preparing CSPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiol‐ene reaction is an effective approach to prepare novel CSPs with well‐defined molecular structure, which is of great importance to the design of new CD‐CSP.
this CD‐CPS is suitable for separation of racemic compounds by HPLC.

the phenyl carbamate group on the rims of β‐CD could extend the cavity size of the CD, and also improve the π‐π interaction, dipole–dipole interaction and hydrogen bonding interaction between CD and the analytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phenyl carbamate group can be used as a new functional group for the synthesis of CD‐CPSs.
the thiol‐ene “click” reaction is an effective method to synthesize CD‐CSP, and the synthesized CD‐CSP can be used for chiral separation.
thiol‐alkene click chemistry can be used as a versatile tool for the preparation of new CD‐CSP.
